recognize_zh: 骨髓抹片鐵染色（Prussian blue）中，多顆紅血球系前驅細胞核周出現藍色鐵顆粒排列成環狀或部分環狀，另見一顆含大量藍色鐵的巨噬細胞；核周環狀鐵顆粒即環狀鐵粒母細胞（ring sideroblast）。
features: Erythroid precursors with coarse blue siderotic granules arranged around the nucleus (ring sideroblasts)
Additional precursors with scattered, non-ring siderotic granules
Iron-laden macrophage with confluent blue cytoplasmic iron (lower center)
Image is slightly out of focus, limiting granule counting at this magnification
describe_en: Prussian blue iron stain of the bone marrow aspirate shows numerous erythroid precursors containing coarse siderotic granules, several of which encircle a substantial portion of the nucleus, consistent with ring sideroblasts. Storage iron is present within a macrophage. Focus and magnification limit precise enumeration in this field. Findings are consistent with increased ring sideroblasts, supporting a diagnosis of myelodysplastic/myeloproliferative neoplasm with ring sideroblasts and thrombocytosis in the appropriate context.

ddx.vs: Normal sideroblasts contain only a few fine scattered granules, whereas ring sideroblasts have at least 5 granules covering at least one-third of the nuclear circumference.

ddx.dx: Acquired sideroblastic anemia from copper deficiency, alcohol or drugs (isoniazid, linezolid)
ddx.vs: Morphology is identical; clinical history and reversibility after removing the cause, without clonal SF3B1 mutation, distinguish these.
Artifactual deposits lie off-cell or over the whole slide rather than forming a consistent perinuclear ring within erythroid precursors.
